title: A ring map inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra is a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms, and the same with residue field isomorphisms

standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for writing an algebra as a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Sets up the shape of the proof of (1): it suffices to factor every finitely presented algebra mapping to B through a member of the colimit.

standard_prerequisites.name: A subalgebra inherits the property of inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the image of a finitely presented algebra mapping to B still induces a universal homeomorphism, so the criterion can be applied to it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Writing an algebra as a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras with surjective transition maps, and factoring a map from a finitely presented algebra through a member of such a colimit, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the presentation of the image as a colimit of finitely presented algebras and an index through which the given finitely presented algebra factors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reduction of a universal homeomorphism to the associated reduced rings, and the dense image criterion placing the reduced base inside the reduced image, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the argument for the claim be carried out after replacing the rings by their reductions, where the inclusion of the reduced base into the reduced image is available.

standard_prerequisites.name: The structure result for a finite type algebra inducing a universal homeomorphism: generators satisfying square or cube relations, or p-th power relations, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the finite list of generators and relations whose preservation at large indices is what makes the transition algebras induce universal homeomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebra lemmas that maps of p-th power type and of 2-3 type induce universal homeomorphisms on spectra, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that each step of the chain of intermediate algebras, and hence the whole map, induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra.

core_obligations: Prove (1) through the colimit criterion: given a finitely presented A-algebra C with an A-algebra map to B, take its image B', which still induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra by inheritance to subalgebras, write B' as a filtered colimit of finitely presented A-algebras with surjective transition maps, factor C through one of them, and reduce the statement to the claim that for all sufficiently large indices the map on spectra of that member over A is a universal homeomorphism (proof lines 11926-11939).

Prove the claim: pass to reduced rings, use the dense image criterion to obtain an inclusion of the reduced base into the reduced image, replace the base by the image so that the map is injective, apply the structure result for finite type algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms to obtain generators satisfying square or cube relations or p-th power relations, lift those generators to the first member of the colimit, observe that the same relations hold from some index on and that the kernel of the map from A to that member is locally nilpotent, and conclude with the algebra lemmas that the chain of intermediate algebras induces universal homeomorphisms on spectra (proof lines 11944-11980).

Part (2) of the statement, the variant in which the map is also required to induce isomorphisms on residue fields, is disposed of by the author with the sentence that its proof is exactly the same; this deferral is recorded in the editorial notes and is not supplied by this card.
proof_roadmap: Apply the colimit criterion to the image of an arbitrary finitely presented algebra, and prove the resulting largeness claim by reducing to reduced rings, invoking the structure of finite type algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms, lifting the finitely many generators and their relations to a member of the colimit, and applying the p-th power and 2-3 type lemmas (proof lines 11926-11981).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a ring map inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra is a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras with the same property, and likewise with isomorphisms on residue fields added (statement lines 11910-11923). The counted proof runs 57 lines and has two genuinely different layers: the criterion for filtered colimits of finitely presented algebras together with the inheritance of universal homeomorphisms by subalgebras gives the reduction to a largeness claim, and the claim itself is proved by passing to reduced rings, replacing the base by the image of the map, quoting the structure of finite type algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms, and lifting finitely many generators and their square, cube or p-th power relations to a member of the colimit so that the p-th power and 2-3 type lemmas apply (proof lines 11926-11980). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains several checkable constructions and reductions, not a restatement, and the only deferral is part (2), which the author declares to have exactly the same proof as the fully proved part (1).
